Match the TV\'s refresh rate to the video (24/25/50/60 fps) in full screen, for Live TV and VOD, and restore it on exit. Turn off if your TV or receiver re-handshakes HDMI noisily on every channel change.
What Live TV, Movies and Series return to when you come back.
This category has too many items for one bulk rename — rename it in smaller spans.
How catch-up timestamps are sent. Automatic uses the time zone your provider\'s server reports, or your device\'s if it reports none. You can also choose Device, or set the offset yourself.
Choose what to remove for this profile. Playlists, favorites and downloads are not affected.
Override the city used for weather. Leave blank to auto-detect, or enter a city (e.g. London) or \"lat,lon\" (e.g. 51.5,-0.12). Useful on a VPN, where auto-detect resolves to the server\'s city.
A combined category for this profile — move channels, movies or series into it.
Connection refused — check the server address and port.
Enter a DNS server host or a DoH URL.
Custom DNS can help bypass ISP-level domain blocking or enable geo-unblocking via SmartDNS services. DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) is recommended — it encrypts your lookups.
Network is unreachable — check the server address.

Guide column widths
Resize the channel list and EPG timeline in the TV Guide.
Use the TV\'s hardware decoder. Turn off if some streams stutter or show artifacts.
Tints buttons, the focus glow, progress bars and highlights everywhere. Pick a preset, or press OK for the palette and any hex code.

Open the address or scan the code in a browser on any device on the same Wi-Fi — a phone, a computer or another TV — fill in your playlist there and send it here. Much faster than typing a URL with the remote.
Type an Xtream login, an M3U address or a Stalker portal with the remote, then start the import from the panel.

Catch-up plays programs from your provider’s archive. Automatic uses the time zone your provider reports, or your TV’s own clock if it reports none; choose a fixed UTC offset if catch-up still starts at the wrong time. This is also where you choose which player catch-up uses.
Shows your provider’s channel number beside the name in the Live TV list, the channel-list overlay and the player, and lets you type a number on the remote in full screen to jump to that channel.
Hide categories and items you never watch, give categories your own names and put them in your order. Hidden things come back here, never lost.
Looks up your provider’s addresses with a DNS server of your choice instead of your network’s own — useful when your network blocks or redirects them.
Add an EPG source (XMLTV) by its link, re-sync it or remove it. EPG sources fill the TV guide and the programme lines in Live TV.
The ring drawn around whatever has focus. Pick its color and thickness so it stays easy to follow from the sofa.
Pick which rows Home shows and in what order, and how the Now trending row looks.
Uses the TV’s hardware decoder: smooth 4K and less heat. Turn it off only if some streams stutter or show blocks; the software decoder then does the work.
The focused channel plays in the preview beside the Live TV list, so you see what is on before you open it. Needs a layout with room for the preview.
The small player that keeps a channel going in a corner while you browse. Choose its size and the corner it sits in.
The address of your .m3u or .m3u8 list.
Add a playlist from a link, an Xtream login, a Stalker portal or a file, re-sync one, or remove it.
Ask to resume offers Resume or Start over when a film or episode has a saved position. Always resume carries on where you stopped; Never resume starts from the beginning.
Subtitles in this language are switched on by themselves when a stream has them. Otherwise subtitles stay off until you pick a track in the player.
The volume every channel, film and episode starts at. Above 100%% quiet streams are amplified. A volume you change in the player is kept for that title until you reset it.
Shows the temperature and your town next to the clock. Set a location by hand when the automatic one is wrong — behind a VPN, for example — and choose Celsius or Fahrenheit.
Enter 6 hex digits, e.g. 52DBC8
Hidden sections stay listed so you can turn them back on.

The Live TV Preview panel is hidden. Give it a width above 0%% in Panel Width Adjustment before turning Preview video on.
Leave blank to auto-detect from your public IP. Enter a city (e.g. London) or \"lat,lon\" (e.g. 51.5,-0.12).
Your shared allowance
Enter a title to look up.
Open the address in a browser on any device — a phone, a computer or another TV — sign in to TMDB there, and send the key across. Nothing to type with the remote.
Daily metadata share used up — add your own TMDB key in Settings → Metadata to remove this limit.
Use only what your playlist provides. No TMDB lookups.
Your playlist\'s info wins; TMDB fills the gaps and adds cast, genres & backdrops.

Leave both blank to use the built-in shared server (no setup). Enter your own TMDB API key to call TMDB directly, or a self-hosted server URL to use your own proxy/mirror. A URL takes priority over a key.
Choose where Movies & Series details come from.
Prefer TMDB for every field; fall back to your playlist only when TMDB has nothing.
The small floating player you get when you dock (PiP) a channel while browsing. Change these here, or on the fly with the resize / move buttons on the mini-player itself.
The item leaves “%1$s” unless you keep it there.
Watch several live channels at once. You choose how many each time, up to this limit — every tile uses one of your provider\'s connections.
Fill in your details in a browser on another device on the same Wi-Fi — a phone, a computer or another TV.
Live Preview video is currently on. Hiding the Preview panel will turn the video off, and it cannot be turned on again until you give the Preview panel a width in Panel Width Adjustment.
The last crash and the most recent playback failures (newest first). Include these details when reporting a problem.
Enter a valid host and port (1–65535).
Your proxy provider can see which servers you connect to, and the contents of any non-HTTPS traffic.

Adds a record button to the player that saves the channel you are watching. It fetches the channel itself, so it uses one of your provider’s connections while it runs, and it keeps recording after you change channel or leave the player.

Recording fetches the channel a second time, so it uses another of your provider’s connections. On an account that allows only one, the recording is refused while you are watching. Once started it keeps going on its own — change channel, leave the player, and it carries on until the programme ends or you stop it from Recordings.
The details appear here; you press Start import with the remote.
